analysis.title: Equity Correlation Rises / Bull Market Intact / SPX Capitulation Signals
key_insights: Desk sees a US rotation story turning into a correlation story: index-level moves are now appearing on top of sector rotations already underway. If correlation keeps rising, the sell-off moves from crowded sectors and relative-value positions into broad portfolio risk.
Wayne Gouro says to largely park fundamentals. Memory fell 16% on Thursday but is still up 78% on the year, and positioning matters more than absolute prices at this point.

Versus July, buyers are missing. July's sell-off was short because CTAs, retail and long-only accounts that missed the first AI leg absorbed the deleveraging. The desk does not see that demand yet, even though the leverage starting point is cleaner today.

Desk argues for support in rest-of-world versus US markets given a potential shift in the political and geopolitical landscape. The 'Trump put' is described as more of a tailwind for RoW through potentially lower oil than for broader Tech.

UBS Knowledge Network technicals (Jason Perl) call Thursday's sell-off corrective rather than the end of the bull market. Risk/reward is skewed higher into year-end, supporting an eventual SPX target of 8,485 next year.

SOX daily and weekly TD Propulsion downside targets were reached Thursday. 63.3% of constituents are at or near DeMark Buy signals and a TD Combo 13 Buy could trigger as soon as Monday. Initial recovery levels are 9,264 and 9,530, and 9,938 would relieve the immediate downside threat. NDX is about one day behind.

Derivatives strategist Rebecca Cheong expects SPX to establish a low on Monday after three capitulation signals: record $365bn excess sell flow, UBS RMM flow buying the dip at the 68th percentile versus 3y after the largest selling episode since covid, and a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 96%.

Systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210bn on Thursday: Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn, CTA $25-30bn. The desk estimates Risk Control could sell another $200-270bn over the next two days, then Risk Control and CTA flows become very small after Monday.
Client conversations on Thursday were not shocked, with substantial interest in deploying capital into weakness rather than broad capitulation.

UBS industrials analyst Amit Mehrota says the market may be conflating data centre regulation with a halt. The AI-exposed industrial selloff followed the Democratic midterm sweep, including governor wins in Texas and Georgia where incoming governors have advocated moratoriums on new data centre approvals. The policy debate is moving toward self-reliance on power, grid and water, which affects electrical and thermal infrastructure suppliers differently.

US payrolls preview: economist Jonathan Pingle lifted the October nonfarm payroll forecast modestly to 75K (private +75K, government flat) after initial claims fell 6K to 189K. A New York unemployment-insurance outage should depress claims for two weeks, then cause a catch-up rebound.
Q3 productivity rose 3.6% annualized, unit labour costs fell 0.7% annualized and rose 2.4% y/y. UBS reads labour as not the main inflation threat and sees gradual labour-market cooling.

Banxico unexpectedly cut 25bp to 6.25% in a 3-2 vote versus a hold expected, but called it a 'one-off adjustment' and said holding for a 'prolonged period' would help convergence. The signal is a recalibration, not an automatic cutting cycle. USDMXN hit 18.95 and was back at 18.82.

Germany September industrial production rose 0.7% m/m and 0.4% y/y, beating the -0.1% m/m consensus but missing the +1.2% y/y forecast. Factory orders rose 4.4% m/m and October manufacturing PMI was 54.2, but September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m against a +0.4% consensus.

About 575,000 people protested across France on Thursday, the largest since September, as the budget standoff deepens. The National Assembly rejected the 2027 budget revenue measures 458-0, a Senate vote is expected Dec 9, and the government could use Article 49.3, ordinances after Dec 17, or a special rollover law.

New Zealand election is Saturday. Labour is at 30.7% versus National at 26.4% in the Post/Freshwater Strategy poll, and Opportunity at 5.1% could decide the next government. UBS economist Stephen Wu sees a macro fork for RBNZ policy between a National-led and a Labour-led coalition.
Japan September average cash earnings rose 4.6% y/y, the fastest since January 1997, versus 3.8% expected, supporting the case for further BoJ hikes. The market expects the next move in December.

Japan's GPIF lost 1.7% in the three months through September and left strategic allocation targets at 25% each, giving little evidence of imminent JPY repatriation. Near term, safe-haven demand and narrowing rate differentials support JPY.

BoJ plans to raise annual ETF sales to JPY860bn from JPY330bn starting January. PM Takaichi said extra proceeds should be reinvested in sectors critical to economic expansion, and she faces a year-end deadline to explain funding for defense spending and a two-year food sales tax cut.

Rates flow: a December Fed hike is priced at 66%, down from 81% on Wednesday. The desk saw 2-5y buying, 50k Week 1 TY 107.50/108 call spreads bought, and a buyer of 35k SFRZ6 95.9375/96.0625/96.1875 call flies positioned for a Fed pass in December.

FX shows a risk-off pattern from the tech sell-off: USD firmer, CHF and JPY supported, commodity currencies weakest. EURUSD support is at 1.1180, then 1.1100/10, with resistance at 1.1215/20 and 1.1260/70.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS technicals call Thursday's selloff corrective, not the end of the bull market. Three capitulation signals triggered, the desk expects an SPX low on Monday as systematic selling fades, and there is client interest in buying weakness.
tension_points.bear_case: Correlation is rising, long-only buyers who absorbed the July deleveraging have not appeared, and Risk Control could sell another $200-270bn over the next two days.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A TD Combo 13 Buy on SOX has not yet triggered, and 9,938 on SOX would relieve the immediate downside threat. Systematic selling that does not fade after Monday would weaken the low-on-Monday call.
